findings.evidence: QuarkPart.lean:109 `quarkPart_def` is the only restatement; `quarkKinetic` by contrast has both `quarkKinetic_apply` (:96) and `quarkKinetic_apply_of_isHermitian` (:136).
findings.fix: Add `quarkPart_apply : quarkPart β γ ψ Dψ μ ν = (quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ μ ν + quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ ν μ) / 2` and the Hermitian working form `quarkPart_apply_of_isHermitian (hγ) : quarkPart β γ ψ Dψ μ ν = ((star ψ ⬝ᵥ (β * γ μ) *ᵥ (I • Dψ ν)).re + (star ψ ⬝ᵥ (β * γ ν) *ᵥ (I • Dψ μ)).re) / 2`, mirroring `quarkKinetic_apply` / `quarkKinetic_apply_of_isHermitian`.
findings.issue: `quarkPart` has only the matrix-level `quarkPart_def`; there is no entrywise lemma, so the physics form advertised in its docstring and in the module header, `T_q{}_{μν} = (1/4) ψ̄ (γ_μ i D↔_ν + γ_ν i D↔_μ) ψ`, is stated nowhere as a lemma. A consumer wanting an entry must unfold through `quarkPart_def` plus `smul_apply`/`add_apply`/`transpose_apply`, and then again through `quarkKinetic`.

findings.evidence: QuarkPart.lean:95-99 (`@[simp] lemma quarkKinetic_apply`) vs QuarkPart.lean:136-138 (`quarkKinetic_apply_of_isHermitian`), identical LHS `quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ μ ν`.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `quarkKinetic_apply`, keeping it as a plain `(rfl)` lemma; the file's own proofs already cite it explicitly via `simp only`/`rw` (lines 127, 139, 151, 171), so nothing else breaks.
findings.issue: `@[simp]` on `quarkKinetic_apply` makes the raw complex expression `(I * (… - …)).re / 2` the simp-normal form of every entry. `quarkKinetic_apply_of_isHermitian` has the same LHS, so the lemma the module header advertises as the working form competes with the default simp set and gets rewritten away in any `simp` call.

findings.evidence: QuarkPart.lean:197-199 `@[simp] lemma diracOp_def`; used as hypothesis at QuarkPart.lean:227 and Total.lean:112, and in the RHS at QuarkPart.lean:214 and Total.lean:101.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `diracOp_def` (keep the `(rfl)` lemma); cite it explicitly where needed, as `trace_inv_mul_quarkKinetic` already does.
findings.issue: `@[simp]` on `diracOp_def` unfolds the Dirac operator by default, but `diracOp` is exactly the term the trace API is phrased in: it is the RHS of `trace_quarkPart`/`trace_total` and the hypothesis shape `h : diracOp g γ Dψ = M *ᵥ ψ` of `trace_quarkPart_of_diracEq`/`trace_total_of_diracEq`. Any `simp` on such a goal or hypothesis erases `diracOp`, after which those theorems no longer match.

summary: The surface is minimal and correctly scoped, but the headline definition `quarkPart` has no entrywise characteristic lemma, and `@[simp]` on `quarkKinetic_apply` and `diracOp_def` makes the simp-normal form clobber the file's own working forms (`quarkKinetic_apply_of_isHermitian`) and the `diracOp` hypothesis shape used by the trace theorems.
